- `defaultNumeral` (`impls/Functionals.scala`): an expression whose type is `IntLiteral` or `FloatLiteral` becomes a coercion to `ZZ32`, or `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, or `RR64`, through `numeralReading` and `coercions.buildCoercion`. It is applied:
  - at an untyped binding, top level and local, one variable or several (`impls/Decls.scala`, the four sites the review names);
  - at a parameter that the numeral fits without conversion, `Any`, `Object`, `Number`, where the default fits too (`defaultAtUnfixed`): in `checkApplicableWithoutInference`, in its `AnyType` domain branch (a lone `Any` parameter skipped the argument loop), and after inference in the coercion attempt;
  - at a static argument that numerals alone fix: such a parameter's candidate types are the default alone (no context) or no literal type (with a context), a numeral at a bare static parameter takes its default before the subtyping inference (no context), and a subtyping inference that still yields a literal static argument is refused so that the coercion attempt reads it;
  - at a dotted receiver written as a numeral, `(3).zero`, where the default type has the member (`defaultReceiver`); where it has not, the numeral stays, because the prelude itself writes `(1).asNN32` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:812`, `:814`) and `ZZ32` there has no `asNN32`;
  - at a tie (`numeralTie`): each numeral read at its default, the candidates that the arguments so read fit without coercion, then those where only the numerals' positions fit without it.
- The default ranks as no coercion: `counted` (`Functionals.scala`) and `moreSpecificCandidate` (`useful/STypesUtil.scala`) skip a coercion that `LiteralDefaults` made.
- A typed place whose type declares no coercion from the literal type but one from its default takes the default, then that coercion (`viaDefault` in `CoercionOracle.buildCoercion`). This is what lets a program's own type take a numeral (section 6).
- `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` cannot be written outside the library's own files (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala`): "IntLiteral cannot be written in a program: a numeral has its own type only while the checker types the program." A file counts as the library's when its path holds `/Library/` or `/LibraryBuiltin/`; a type is written by the program when its span's file is the unit's own.
- Joins (`if`, `case`) are not built: an untyped binding of a join of numerals coerces the whole expression, so its branches still make literal values.

== Specification/basic/inference.tex:299-437

\section{A Numeral Whose Conversions Tie}
\seclabel{numeral-default}

A numeral has a type of its own, from which \library\ define coercions to the
number types (\secref{literals}).
Where the types to which a numeral can be converted are incomparable under
$\morespecificeq$, as \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} are, each
taking a numeral and neither converting into the other, the numeral is read as
a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, or as a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} when its
value does not fit in the narrower type.
This holds in either step: in the choice among declarations that are applicable
to the call only with coercion and that the numeral would otherwise leave tied,
and in the instantiation of a type parameter that only numerals fix.
So of the declarations \EXP{g(x\COLON\mathbb{N}32)} and
\EXP{g(x\COLON\mathbb{Z}32)}, the call \EXP{g(0)} invokes the second; and a
type parameter that only numerals fix, whose bounds \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} satisfy and the numeral's own type does not, is
instantiated at \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} when \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} holds the numerals'
values.

The rule settles only a tie that a numeral makes.
Where an argument that is not a numeral leaves the declarations applicable to a
call only with coercion tied, no declaration is the most specific, and the call
is a static error.

This chapter does not yet describe:
\begin{itemize}
\item the static arguments of a \KWD{bool}, \KWD{dim}, \KWD{unit} or operator
parameter (\secref{boolparams}, \secref{dimunitparams}, \secref{opr-ident});
\item a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter that neither an argument nor the
expected type fixes;
\item the element type of a reduction that only its generator clauses determine
(\secref{reduction-expr}): the rule above gives a static parameter of the big
operator that nothing at the call fixes its bounds, not the type of the
elements;
\item whether an argument whose declared parameter type mentions a static
parameter inside another type may be converted where only a conversion of its
elements would satisfy the bounds of the parameter; under the rule above such
an argument fixes the parameter by subtyping and is not converted;
\item an expected type in any context other than those listed above, such as
the body of a \KWD{for} loop;
\item the static arguments of an object with static parameters that is named
without a call, which a program writes (\secref{where-clauses});
\item the inference over a whole program of the types that declarations elide
(\secref{type-inference-components}).
\end{itemize}
\revision{revival-expected-contexts}{The revival's text of 29~September 2026
named here also an expression that a local declaration precedes in a block, an
\KWD{if} expression without an \KWD{else} clause, a \KWD{typecase} expression
and a call written by loose juxtaposition, its text of 8~October 2026 also
the body of a \KWD{label} expression, and its text of 9~October 2026 also an
argument of another call, to which the list of contexts in
\secref{static-arg-inference} now gives an expected type where the argument is
itself a call with inferred static arguments and the enclosing call
is not accepted without it.}
\revision{revival-inference}{The compiled type checker instantiates a type
parameter that neither an argument nor the expected type fixes at the
intersection of its upper bounds, as \secref{static-arg-inference} says; on the
compiled path, as in the interpreter, a type parameter declared without an
\KWD{extends} clause is bounded by \TYP{Any}, so that a call that fixes such a
parameter by the expected type alone may fix it at a type that \TYP{Object}
excludes, such as \TYP{()}.
A reduction's big operator is an argument of the call that the reduction's
desugaring makes, so it has an expected type only as such an argument has one:
the compiled type checker instantiates a generic big operator whose static
argument the reduction does not write at its bound, and at the reduction's
expected type only where the reduction's type at that bound does not fit it,
and it refuses the reduction where the big operator has no instance at its
bound, as one whose bound mentions its own static parameter has none (row~425
of the revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter instantiates a type parameter of a function that nothing at a
call fixes at its bound, \TYP{Any} if it has none, and one whose bound mentions
other static parameters at that bound with their instances, with two
exceptions: a type parameter that only the bound of a type parameter that the
arguments fix mentions, as \EXP{A \KWD{extends} T} mentions \VAR{T}, it
instantiates at the arguments' type, not at its bound, since it has no expected
type to fix it (row~592 of the revival's gap ledger); and a type parameter
declared with several bounds that it cannot meet, as two bounds neither of which
is a subtype of the other, it erases to \TYP{BottomType} (row~591).
A type parameter whose bound mentions the type parameter itself, as the big
operators $\sum$ and $\prod$ declare theirs, and that nothing at a call fixes,
it leaves open: it does not instantiate it, and it admits every value where it
checks a value against that type, as an argument, a variable declared with that
type, a \KWD{typecase} clause or a type assertion.
The big operator that a reduction or a comprehension invokes without its
static arguments it instantiates as the desugaring by the type \VAR{N} of the
expression would (\secref{reduction-expr}), with run-time types in place of the
static type that it does not have: by the declared type of the local variable,
or the declared return type of the top-level or local function, whose value the
reduction or the comprehension is, also as the last expression of a block, where
that type fixes the big operator's result type; otherwise by the join of the run-time types of
the elements that its generator clauses give, which it collects before it
reduces them; and where there is no element, at the bound of each static
parameter, or open where the bound mentions the parameter itself.
So an empty sum that is the value of a function declared \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}
is the \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} zero, and the library's set reductions
\EXP{\bigcup} and \EXP{\bigcap} run on sets of their elements' type; but an
empty reduction that no declared type directs takes the identity of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} whatever the type of the expression, and an empty
comprehension that no declared type directs is built at the bound, a list
comprehension as a \EXP{\TYP{List}\llbracket\TYP{Any}\rrbracket} (row~716 of the
revival's gap ledger); a comprehension that no declared type reaches, such as
the value of a top-level variable, a field, a method or a function expression,
the right-hand side of an assignment, the body of another reduction or an
argument of a call, is
built at the run-time types of its elements, which the declared type of an
enclosing expression may not admit (rows~20, 510 and~717).
A big operator whose declared result is none of the library's
\TYP{BigReduction}, \TYP{Comprehension} and \TYP{BigOperator} it instantiates
through the one of those three that its declared result extends, with that
trait's static arguments.
It gives a function expression that declares no return type the return type
\TYP{BottomType}, so that a type parameter that only its result fixes is
instantiated there (row~587); and it instantiates a static parameter of a
generic method that only the expected type would fix, as one of a generic
function, at its bound (row~510), a method that a trait declares among them.
The third item of the team's draft note below asks whether inference may give a
static parameter \TYP{BottomType}; the rule of \secref{static-arg-inference},
taken from the type group's paper of 2019, answers that it may not.
Neither implementation infers a \KWD{bool} parameter yet: the compiled type
checker refuses by name to infer a \KWD{bool}, \KWD{dim} or \KWD{unit}
parameter, and the interpreter does not unify a \KWD{bool} one (row~307 of
the revival's gap ledger) and stops at load on an object or trait whose method
has a parameter type with a \KWD{bool} static argument (row~761).
The example of \secref{boolparams}, a coercion whose \KWD{bool} parameter only
its parameter type mentions, can be applied only if its argument fixes that
parameter.}

\note{ \begin{itemize}
 \item
 There seems to be a circular dependency between inference and juxtaposition
 disambiguation -- you have to know if the subexpressions have arrow types
 to disambiguate, but you can't do that without using inference, which
 requires knowing how the variable of unknown type is used.
\item Type Inference (Dan's email titled ``Comments on a first reading of the spec'' on 06/05/07)
\item Do we want to forbid such cases where type inference infers
\TYP{BottomType}s for static parameters?
 \end{itemize}
}

**For the whole batch**

1. **Six rungs, N, C, F, G, S, T, in the manifest's order; C lands only with N; T lands only with N, C, F and S.** Default: so. The way not taken: PLAN's split by area, with walk's numerals in a rung of their own landing with the library's, which no worker could build on the base's library (section 2, reason 1).

# Reading B, built: a numeral's default on the compiled path

**What was asked.** Build reading B's compiled side as `explorations/reviews/literal-fork-2026-11-08.md` §4.2 and §6.3 (rungs 2 to 4) lay it out, in four steps, measuring after each, with test programs written first; then measure the lines, the count and distance stages, the checker's time, the compiled suites, the walk suite after the library change, the library's own numerals that the default retypes, and microGPT. The coordinator added, during the work: a program's own number type (`CC64`), an interval type, a bfloat16 type, and, by reading, a hybrid that lets a program's type receive a numeral's exact value (sections 6 and 7).

**Trees, tools, files.**
- Base: `8cde0b2c4f`, main's head when the work started. The base build is `/home/user/fortress-base29`, made by `references/worktrees.md` (`ant compileAll` 50 s, the library order, `bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss`, `git status --porcelain` empty, 282 MB). `df -P /home/user` before it: 21,477,916 KB available. It is kept for batch 29.
- The prototype ran in `/home/user/fortress-proto-b`, seeded from it by `seed-worktree.sh` in 4 s, and only there. The worktree and its caches are removed; the patch keeps the code.
- Machine for every run: `nproc` 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz, OpenJDK 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` except the suites (4).
- The checker against the one library was read through the count stage's driver, `explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/WorldFlip.java`, with `-stop check`, as the review did (§3.1); a static type is read from a refused binding `s: String = e`.
- The prototype prints where it applied a default when the environment sets `FORTRESS_LITERAL_TRACE` (`LiteralDefaults` in `Functionals.scala`, in the patch): one line `LITERAL-DEFAULT <span> <type> at <place>` for each default that the checked component keeps. Section 5 is built from those lines.
- Java and Scala paths are under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/`. Every claim about the prototype's code cites the patch; lines in `Library/` are the worktree's after the step named.

## 1. What I built, step by step

The steps are cumulative. The lines are `git diff --stat` in the worktree after each step (section 3.1 gives the areas).

### Step 1, the library: `FloatLiteral` apart, its coercions, the float tie rule, the literal `=` pairs dropped

- `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi` and `.fss`: `value object FloatLiteral extends RR64` becomes `value object FloatLiteral extends Number`, which declares its own `asFloat(self): Float` (P-165). It stays an object, not the prelude's trait: walk makes `FFloatLiteral` values through its native constructor `interpreter/glue/prim/FloatLiteral.java` and calls its three glue bindings (section 4.5). An object excludes every type it does not extend, so `excludes { RR32, RR64 }` holds without the clause.
- `RR64` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, `.fss`): `comprises { Float }`, and `coerce(x: FloatLiteral) = asFloat(x)`, one rounding (walk's `FFloatLiteral.getFloat` is `Double.valueOf` of the text).
- `QQ`: `coerce(x: FloatLiteral) = numeralRatio(x.asString)`, exact: a new private function of 14 lines reads the decimal text into `n / d`.
- `RR32`: `coerce(x: FloatLiteral) = narrow(asFloat(x))`. Under walk this rounds twice; the compiled path folds it with one rounding (step 3). One rounding under walk needs a float parse of the text, which no helper has (`nativeHelpers` has `simpleDoubleArith.parseDouble` only).
- The `=` pairs over the literal types dropped, 15 in each of the api and the component: `RR64`'s, `QQ`'s, `ZZ32`'s, `ZZ64`'s, `NN64`'s, `ZZ`'s and `NN32`'s `opr =(self, b: IntLiteral)`, and `IntLiteral`'s own eight. No `=` pair over `FloatLiteral` was added.
- The float tie rule, in the checker (`impls/Functionals.scala`, `isNumeral` and `numeralReading`): a numeral with a radix point counts as a numeral at a tie and reads as `RR64`. I put it in step 1 because the library change alone makes ties (step 1a below).
- `Float`'s `asFloat(self)` returns `RR64` instead of `Float` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:82`): with `RR64` comprising `Float` alone the checker reads the two domains as equal and asks each return type to fit the other (step 1b below).
- Lines: 5 files, +46 −41 (the library 4 files, the checker's tie rule 19 lines of `Functionals.scala`).

### Step 2, the checker: the default at each kind of place, the literal types unwritable

### Step 3, the fold

- `compiler/desugarer/IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.java` (the phase before the checker): an expression of numerals alone folds exactly into one numeral, the Working Draft's static expressions (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/constant.tex`, "Static Expressions"; `literals.tex:163-173`): `+`, `-`, multiplication, `/` by a nonzero numeral, `^` by an integer numeral (an integer base takes no negative exponent; exponents beyond 4096 do not fold), and a prefix `-` on a float numeral. A result that IEEE arithmetic could make a negative zero does not fold, so `-0.0` stays `-(0.0)` (`StrictEquivalenceRuleCompiled` asserts `0.0` and `-0.0` are not `SEQV`). A result with a radix point, or a quotient, is a numeral with a radix point: in decimal where the denominator divides a power of ten (`10.0^(-5)` becomes `0.00001`), else with the denominator as its base (`1/3`). The visitor's earlier integer folds (comparisons, `DIV`, `MIN`) stay.

Section 5's string-juxtaposition sites are of this kind.
- **The 12 other components'** default sites: `WorldFlip` given the 14 files in one run printed only `FortressLibrary`'s (81 lines), and the distance stage printed none of the trace (its run captures standard error, but no `LITERAL-DEFAULT` line appeared); I traced `String` alone and did not run the other 12 one by one.
- **The demos** (`tests-running.md`, "Outside the gate") were not run: the library change edits walk's library, and walk's float ties already fail 71 tests, so the driver's verdict would carry no news about B.
- **The specification's text** for B (review §5.3) is not written: this is a prototype.
- **Timing beyond the smoke test**: no profile, no second pass.

## 9. Defects found

- **The `=` pairs over `IntLiteral` dropped breaks the one library's comparisons with a numeral under A, and `NN32`'s, `NN64`'s and `RR32`'s against an integer numeral under B**, by reading (section 5). A defect of the brief's sub-choice, not of the tree; under B it needs either the pairs kept and folded, or `=` pairs from `ZZ32` into the unsigned types, which P-74 forbids as implicit coercions. Recorded here only: no gated test can show it before the switch-over (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded", item 3; its row is for the curator's decision, below).
- **`InferO2Pos:18`, `:19` choose the declaration with the `ZZ32` parameter**, not the review's predicted one over `Any` (4.3). Not isolated: it may be B's correct answer (the numeral is a `ZZ32`) or a side effect of the step-2 tie rule or the pre-default at a bare static parameter.
- **Walk loads `FloatLiteral` apart from `RR64` with no float tie rule**, so 71 tests fail (4.5); predicted by both readings' rung 2, measured here.
- Defects of the prototype found and repaired on the way, each by a measured failure: the unwritable check firing on the prelude's own generated names and on relative library paths ("Internally generated library name ... IntLiteral cannot be written in a program"); the default at `Any` ranking as a coercion (count 38); `Cell(0.5)` taking `RR32` as the narrowest candidate; a lone `Any` parameter skipping the default; the expected type ignored by the pre-default (`InferCoercionShapes:74`, `:76`, `InferLooseJuxtContext:12`, `InferCallArgumentContext:15`, all passing after the repair); the receiver default refusing the prelude's `(1).asNN32`.
- No new ledger row: the patch is not landed, and row 946 (which B resolves) and rows 362, 506 and 862 (which the patch changes) are the record's already.

## 10. Decisions (mine; no decision of the curator covers them)

1. `FloatLiteral` stays a `value object` extending `Number`, not the prelude's trait, because walk's run-time values need an object (4.5). Alternative: a trait with walk's object below it, which walk's native constructor does not support by reading.
2. The receiver default applies only where the default type has the member, so the prelude's `(1).asNN32` keeps compiling with a literal receiver. Alternative: the default always, which needs the prelude edited, against `compiler.md`.
3. A typed place whose type has no coercion from the literal type takes the default and then its own coercion (`viaDefault`), a chain of two conversions for numerals only. Alternative: refuse `c: CC64 = 3` unless `CC64` names the literal type, which B makes unwritable.
4. The fold makes a quotient of numerals a numeral with a radix point, so `x = 7/2` defaults to `RR64`, not `QQ`. Alternative: a folded quotient defaults to `QQ`; then `1/2 = 0.5` compares a `QQ` with an `RR64` and is `false` unless the fold also folds the comparison.
5. A float numeral whose fold could give `-0.0` does not fold.
6. Step 5, a numeral's coercion into its own default ranking as none, was added after the brief's four steps because section 5 showed the library's `ZZ` comparisons at the `=` over `Any`; it is measured on its own.
7. The literal types count as written by the library in any file under `Library/` or `LibraryBuiltin/`; `Library/Constants.fsi:16-17` (`pi: FloatLiteral`) keeps its type, so `pi` is a literal value at run time under B. Alternative: `pi: RR64`.

## 11. Questions for the curator (decisions not taken)

1. **The `=` pairs over the literal types.** Sources: P-165 and P-172 give each coercion its pair; the brief drops the pairs over the literal types under B. Ways: (a) drop them, as built: `u = 0` for `u: NN32`, `NN64` or `RR32` answers `false` (section 5); (b) keep them, and fold the pair's conversion of a numeral into a constant, so that no literal value reaches run time (the review §3.6's second sub-choice); (c) drop them and declare `=` pairs from `ZZ32` into `NN32` and `NN64` without a coercion. Today's behaviour (A, base) keeps them.
2. **`gg(5, w)` and `ee(5)`** (`InferO2Pos:18`, `:19`): under B, does the declaration with a `ZZ32` parameter run (as built), or the one over `Any` (the review's prediction, P-49's wording)? Today: the one over `Any`.
3. **A program's own number type.** Ways: B as built (coercions from the default types; a 20-digit numeral arrives exact as a `ZZ`, a float numeral as a double, section 6); the hybrid of 7.1 (the literal types writable as a coercion's parameter, 4 or 5 of the 24 bindings kept, the accessors added); the Working Draft's static-parameter design of 7.2 (no literal value at run time, a size kind beyond 32 bits, a boolean `where` form); or A. Today, on the compiled path, a program's type receives an integer numeral exactly and a float numeral only as a double (6); on walk, exactly.
4. **`x = 7/2`** with the fold: `RR64` (as built) or `QQ` (today's one library).
5. **`IntLiteral` writable.** As built, unwritable: 9 team tests and 10 of the revival's break (4.3), and the team's `XXXApplicationErrors`, `XXX6at` and `XXX6bw` pinned texts change. Today: writable.

## Summary

I built reading B's compiled side in a worktree seeded from the new base build `/home/user/fortress-base29` (`8cde0b2c4f`, kept), in four steps and a fifth: `FloatLiteral` apart in the one library, with exact and one-rounding coercions and the literal `=` pairs dropped; the checker's default at untyped bindings, `Any` parameters, numeral-fixed static arguments, receivers and ties, the literal types unwritable; the fold of numeral expressions and of a numeral's coercion into a constant rounded once; `IntLiteral`'s 21 glue bindings removed; a numeral's own default ranking as no coercion. The new tests fail on the base and pass after step 3.

Measured:
- Count and distance: 0 and 0 at the base and after each step's final code; the library alone gave 2 ties and then a return-type error, both repaired in step 1. The checker's time: 122 s at the base, 112 s after.
- Lines: the checker +219 −25, the fold +206 −5, the library +39 −139.
- Compiled suites (1475/86/263 passing before): at the end 27 compiler and 4 library failures, none from the fold. The predicted flips occur (`InferCoercionShapes:72`, `InferO2Num:20`, `XXXApplicationErrors`, seven team tests); beyond them, two more team tests writing `IntLiteral`, two pinned messages, ten revival tests naming it in a helper, `XXXInferComboCap` and `XXXNumeralPrintRungR` red (rows 506, 362), and `InferO2Pos` choosing otherwise than predicted.
- Walk after the library change alone: 71 of 791 fail, for want of a float tie rule.
- The library's numerals: 81 default sites in `FortressLibrary`, 65 at the `=` over `Any`; with the pairs dropped A breaks those comparisons, and B breaks `NN32`, `NN64` and `RR32` against an integer numeral (by reading).
- A program's own type under B receives a float numeral as a double: an interval cannot be tight, and bfloat16 double-rounds (`0x3F80` against the exact `0x3F81`, on walk at the base).
- microGPT: all 18 components still stop at name resolution; against the one library the flat program stops at its own `Index` bound.

By reading only: a hybrid keeping the exact value for a program's coercion (4 or 5 of the 24 bindings), and the Working Draft's static-parameter design (no run-time literal value, but a size kind beyond 32 bits and a new `where` form). Unbuilt: joins, `QQ`'s fold, `nat` values, a compiled run on the one library, the specification.

@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+(* Where nothing fixes a type, a numeral takes ZZ32, or ZZ64 or ZZ by its value, and a float numeral RR64: at an untyped binding, a parameter of type Any and a static argument that only the numeral fixes. *)
+component LiteralDefaultCompiled
+export Executable
+
+tName(a: Any): String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.typeName")
+sEq(a: Any, b: Any): Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
+
+object Cell[\T\](v: T) end
+kind(c: Cell[\ZZ32\]): String = "Cell ZZ32"
+kind(c: Cell[\RR64\]): String = "Cell RR64"
+kind(c: Any): String = "other"
+
+f(a: Any): String = tName(a)
+pick[\T\](a: T, b: T): String = tName(a) || "," || tName(b)
+
+g(a: ZZ32): String = "g ZZ32"
+g(a: NN32): String = "g NN32"
+g(a: ZZ64): String = "g ZZ64"
+
+x = 3
+y = 0.5
+bigN = 3000000000
+
+run(): () = do
+  z: ZZ32 = 3
+  w: RR64 = 0.5
+  assert(tName(x), "ZZ32", "x = 3 binds a ZZ32")
+  assert(tName(y), "RR64", "y = 0.5 binds an RR64")
+  lx = 3
+  ly = 0.5
+  assert(tName(lx), "ZZ32", "a local lx = 3 binds a ZZ32")
+  assert(tName(ly), "RR64", "a local ly = 0.5 binds an RR64")
+  assert(tName(bigN), "ZZ64", "bigN = 3000000000 binds a ZZ64")
+  assert(kind(Cell(3)), "Cell ZZ32", "Cell(3) is a Cell of ZZ32")
+  assert(kind(Cell(x)), "Cell ZZ32", "Cell(x) is a Cell of ZZ32")
+  assert(kind(Cell(0.5)), "Cell RR64", "Cell(0.5) is a Cell of RR64")
+  assert(f(3), "ZZ32", "a numeral at a parameter of type Any")
+  assert(f(0.5), "RR64", "a float numeral at a parameter of type Any")
+  assert(pick(3, 4), "ZZ32,ZZ32", "numerals alone fix a static argument")
+  assert(sEq(3, z), "3 SEQV z for z: ZZ32 = 3")
+  assert(sEq(x, z), "x SEQV z")
+  assert(sEq(y, w), "y SEQV w for w: RR64 = 0.5")
+  assert(g(bigN), "g ZZ64", "a variable bound from 3000000000 at a tie of g")
+  assert(g(3000000000), "g ZZ64", "the numeral 3000000000 at a tie of g")
+  println("PASS")
+end
+
+end

+(* An expression of numerals alone folds exactly into one numeral before the checker, and a numeral converts to its type's constant with one rounding of its exact value. *)
+component LiteralFoldCompiled
+export Executable
+
+tName(a: Any): String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.typeName")
+sEq(a: Any, b: Any): Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
+
+run(): () = do
+  assert(tName(3 + 4), "ZZ32", "3 + 4 folds into the numeral 7")
+  assert(3 + 4, 7, "3 + 4 is 7")
+  p = 2^40
+  big: ZZ64 = 1099511627776
+  assert(tName(p), "ZZ64", "2^40 folds into a numeral that takes ZZ64")
+  assert(sEq(p, big), "2^40 is 1099511627776")
+  assert(1/2 = 0.5, "1/2 folds into the numeral 0.5")
+  r: RR64 = 0.77425264282026984
+  assert(r = 0.7742526428202698, "a 17-digit numeral at RR64 rounds once")
+  assert(r > 0.7742526428202697, "a 17-digit numeral at RR64 rounds once, not to the double below")
+  u = 0.77425264282026984
+  assert(sEq(u, r), "an untyped 17-digit numeral rounds once too")
+  println("PASS")
+end
+
+end

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..b7b766809f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LiteralOwnNumberCompiled.fss
@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+(* A program's own number type takes a numeral through coercions from the numeral's default types: an integer numeral arrives as a ZZ32, or a ZZ64 or ZZ by its value, and a float numeral as an RR64, already rounded once to a double, so an interval or a bfloat16 type receives the double, not the numeral's exact value. *)
+component LiteralOwnNumberCompiled
+export Executable
+
+value object CC64(re: RR64, im: RR64, src: String)
+  coerce(x: ZZ32) = CC64(0.0, 0.0, "ZZ32 " || x.asString)
+  coerce(x: ZZ64) = CC64(0.0, 0.0, "ZZ64 " || x.asString)
+  coerce(x: ZZ) = CC64(0.0, 0.0, "ZZ " || x.asString)
+  coerce(x: RR64) = CC64(x, 0.0, "RR64 " || x.asString)
+end
+
+sEq(a: Any, b: Any): Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
+
+value object Iv(lo: RR64, hi: RR64)
+  coerce(x: RR64) = Iv(x, x)
+end
+
+value object BF16(from: RR64)
+  coerce(x: RR64) = BF16(x)
+end
+
+run(): () = do
+  a: CC64 = 3
+  assert(a.src, "ZZ32 3", "an integer numeral arrives as a ZZ32")
+  b: CC64 = 3000000000
+  assert(b.src, "ZZ64 3000000000", "a numeral beyond ZZ32 arrives as a ZZ64")
+  c: CC64 = 12345678901234567890
+  assert(c.src, "ZZ 12345678901234567890", "a 20-digit numeral arrives as a ZZ")
+  d: CC64 = 0.5
+  assert(d.src, "RR64 0.5", "a float numeral arrives as an RR64")
+  e: CC64 = 3.1415926535897932384
+  assert(e.src, "RR64 3.141592653589793", "the Working Draft's numeral arrives rounded once to an RR64")
+  i: Iv = 0.1
+  tenth: RR64 = 0.1
+  assert(sEq(i.lo, tenth), "an interval receives the double nearest 0.1, not 1/10")
+  h: BF16 = 1.00390625000000000001
+  mid: RR64 = 1.00390625
+  assert(sEq(h.from, mid), "a bfloat16 type receives the double 1 + 2^-8, the bfloat16 midpoint, not the numeral above it")
+  println("PASS")
+end
+
+end

content.content:
component IntLiteralArithRung7
export Executable

(*) Rung 7 of the compile-path ladder: the arithmetic operators of IntLiteral
(*) that the compiler world declares and then refuses at run time.
(*)
(*) A binding written without a declared type from an integer literal keeps
(*) the static type IntLiteral on the compile path, so every operator applied
(*) to it resolves to trait IntLiteral's own declaration rather than to a
(*) coerced ZZ32 or ZZ64 one.  Rung 6 gave the six comparisons plus MIN and
(*) MAX real bodies, because each of those either returns a Boolean or returns
(*) one of its two operands.  The arithmetic family was left out of that rung
(*) for one reason: each of its operators returns a new IntLiteral, and the
(*) compiler world has getters out of IntLiteral and no way into it, so the
(*) bodies at ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:816-848 are
(*) still "throw CompilerFailureDetectedAtRunTime".
(*)
(*) The declarations are the published api's, not a local invention:
(*) Specification/library/apis/CompilerBuiltin.tex:374-383 carries the unary
(*) and additive operators of IntLiteral with IntLiteral results.
(*)
(*) This test pins the four operators the blocked programs of
(*) ProjectFortress/tests/ reach -- juxtaposition, unary -, binary - and its
(*) additive partner + -- and pins one chained expression, which shows that
(*) the value a body returns is a usable IntLiteral and not merely something
(*) that prints.
(*)
(*) Every operand is computed at run time by pick(), not written twice as a
(*) literal, and every expected value is computed on the ZZ32 side by pickZZ32
(*) and ZZ32's own arithmetic, which has had real bodies all along.  So a body
(*) that returned a constant, or one that returned its own operand, would not
(*) pass.

(*) Returns 4 or 9 as an IntLiteral, chosen at run time.
pick(b: Boolean): IntLiteral = if b then 4 else 9 end

(*) The same two values as ZZ32, for the expected sides.
pickZZ32(b: Boolean): ZZ32 = if b then 4 else 9 end

run():() = do
    four = pick(true)
    nine = pick(false)

    four32 = pickZZ32(true)
    nine32 = pickZZ32(false)

    assert((four + nine).asZZ32, four32 + nine32, "IntLiteral +: four + nine")
    assert((nine + four).asZZ32, nine32 + four32, "IntLiteral +: nine + four")

    assert((nine - four).asZZ32, nine32 - four32, "IntLiteral -: nine - four")
    assert((four - nine).asZZ32, four32 - nine32, "IntLiteral -: four - nine")

    assert((- four).asZZ32, - four32, "IntLiteral - unary: - four")
    assert((- nine).asZZ32, - nine32, "IntLiteral - unary: - nine")

    assert((four nine).asZZ32, four32 nine32, "IntLiteral juxtaposition: four nine")
    assert((nine four).asZZ32, nine32 four32, "IntLiteral juxtaposition: nine four")

    assert(((four + nine) - four).asZZ32, nine32, "IntLiteral chained: (four + nine) - four")

    println "PASS"
end

end

run

cd /home/user/fortress-numeral-checker/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests && cat > LiteralDefaultCompiled.fss <<'EOF'
(* Where nothing fixes a type, a numeral takes ZZ32, or ZZ64 or ZZ by its value, and a float numeral RR64: at an untyped binding, its tuple's elements and its if or case join's branches, a parameter of type Any, Object or Number, a type parameter that numerals alone fix, at the narrowest default holding them all, and a declaration whose parameter is the default type fits the numeral as it is. *)
component LiteralDefaultCompiled
export Executable

tName(a: Any): String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.typeName")
sEq(a: Any, b: Any): Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")

object Cell[\T\](v: T) end
kind(c: Cell[\ZZ32\]): String = "Cell ZZ32"
kind(c: Cell[\RR64\]): String = "Cell RR64"
kind(c: Any): String = "other"

f(a: Any): String = tName(a)
num(a: Number): String = tName(a)
idT[\T\](a: T): String = tName(a)
pick[\T\](a: T, b: T): String = tName(a) || "," || tName(b)

g(a: ZZ32): String = "g ZZ32"
g(a: NN32): String = "g NN32"
g(a: ZZ64): String = "g ZZ64"

shown(x: Object): String = typecase x of
    ZZ32 => "ZZ32"
    String => "String"
    else => "other"
  end

ee[\nat n\](x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = 1
ee(x: Any): ZZ32 = 2

object Tally(n: ZZ32)
  coerce(x: IntLiteral) = do t = x; Tally(t.asZZ32) end
end

x = 3
y = 0.5
bigN = 3000000000

run(): () = do
  z: ZZ32 = 3
  w: RR64 = 0.5
  assert(tName(x), "ZZ32", "x = 3 binds a ZZ32")
  assert(tName(y), "RR64", "y = 0.5 binds an RR64")
  lx = 3
  ly = 0.5
  assert(tName(lx), "ZZ32", "a local lx = 3 binds a ZZ32")
  assert(tName(ly), "RR64", "a local ly = 0.5 binds an RR64")
  assert(tName(bigN), "ZZ64", "bigN = 3000000000 binds a ZZ64")
  tup = (3, 0.5)
  (tp, tq) = tup
  assert(tName(tp), "ZZ32", "a tuple's integer numeral at an untyped binding binds a ZZ32")
  assert(tName(tq), "RR64", "a tuple's float numeral at an untyped binding binds an RR64")
  flag = z = 3
  j = if flag then 1 else 2 end
  assert(tName(j), "ZZ32", "an if of numerals at an untyped binding is a ZZ32")
  jb = if flag then 1 else 3000000000 end
  assert(tName(jb), "ZZ64", "an if of numerals takes the narrowest default holding every branch")
  jc = case z of
      3 => 7
      else => 8
    end
  assert(tName(jc), "ZZ32", "a case of numerals at an untyped binding is a ZZ32")
  assert(kind(Cell(3)), "Cell ZZ32", "Cell(3) is a Cell of ZZ32")
  assert(kind(Cell(x)), "Cell ZZ32", "Cell(x) is a Cell of ZZ32")
  assert(kind(Cell(0.5)), "Cell RR64", "Cell(0.5) is a Cell of RR64")
  assert(f(3), "ZZ32", "a numeral at a parameter of type Any")
  assert(f(0.5), "RR64", "a float numeral at a parameter of type Any")
  assert(num(3), "ZZ32", "a numeral at a parameter of type Number")
  assert(idT(3), "ZZ32", "a numeral at an unbounded type parameter")
  assert(pick(3, 4), "ZZ32,ZZ32", "numerals alone fix a static argument at their default")
  assert(pick(3, 3000000000), "ZZ64,ZZ64", "several numerals fix a static argument at the narrowest default holding them all")
  assert(sEq(3, z), "3 SEQV z for z: ZZ32 = 3")
  assert(sEq(x, z), "x SEQV z")
  assert(sEq(y, w), "y SEQV w for w: RR64 = 0.5")
  assert(g(bigN), "g ZZ64", "a variable bound from 3000000000 at a tie of g")
  assert(g(3000000000), "g ZZ64", "the numeral 3000000000 at a tie of g")
  assert(shown(7), "ZZ32", "7 at a parameter of type Object takes the ZZ32 clause")
  assert(ee(5), 1, "a declaration whose parameter is the numeral's default type fits it as it is, and the narrower runs")
  a: Any = 5
  assert(tName(a), "ZZ32", "a numeral at a binding of type Any")
  tt: Tally = 3
  assert(tt.n, 3, "a program's coercion from IntLiteral receives the numeral")
  println("PASS")
end

end
EOF
printf 'tests=LiteralDefaultCompiled\nlink\nrun\nrun_out_contains=PASS\n' > LiteralDefaultCompiled.test; cat LiteralDefaultCompiled.test

Climb batch 29 rung C: the checker's numerals, the default where nothing fixes a type, the numeral types written only as a parameter's type, a numeral out of range refused, a size read as a value a ZZ32

Edits the original tree: scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala,
impls/Decls.scala, impls/Misc.scala, CoercionOracle.scala,
TypeWellFormedChecker.scala, STypeChecker.scala, staticenv/KindEnv.scala,
scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala and compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java, and the
team's tests Compiled5.ah, 5.aj, 5.ak, 6.az, 9.g, 9.j, 9.p, 9.t, 9.u and the
pinned texts of XXX6at.test and XXX6bw.test.

- A numeral where nothing fixes a type takes its default, ZZ32, or ZZ64 or ZZ
  by its value, RR64 with a radix point: at an untyped binding, a tuple's
  elements and a join's branches there, a parameter or typed place of type
  Any, Object or Number, a type parameter that numerals alone fix (the
  narrowest default holding them all), a dotted receiver; a numeral's
  coercion into its own default ranks as no coercion (P-173, P-49).
- IntLiteral and FloatLiteral are written in a program only as a parameter's
  type (P-174); a program's type with no coercion from the numeral's type
  refuses a numeral, no chain.
- A numeral outside a bounded number type's range, or rounding to an
  infinity in RR64 or RR32, is refused statically (row 325).
- A nat or int parameter read as a value is a ZZ32, in the checker and the
  code generator (P-40, row 486).
- Tests: LiteralDefaultCompiled, the refusal tests of LiteralTypeUnwritable,
  LiteralNoCoercionRefused and NatValueNN32Refused, NatValueZZ32Compiled,
  NumeralBeyondZZ32Range, NumeralBeyondWidthMax and NumeralPrintRungR
  promoted, XXXInferComboCap rewritten, XXXFloatLiteralValuePrint added,
  tests/NatValueZZ32Walk rewritten from XXXNatValueNN32RungK, and the
  revival's tests that wrote IntLiteral respelled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
EOF
git commit -q -F tmp/rung-numeral-checker/msg1.txt && git log --oneline -1 && git push -q 2>&1 | tail -2; git status -sb | head -3

## 11. Decisions, findings, questions

**Decisions.** No decision of the curator covers 1 to 6.

1. **The split in order (variant B).** Rejected:
   - variant C, which tests `Node` first and skips 213 tests for leaves: 332 s against B's 344 s, one run
     each, within noise; its exactness needs a proof (every node class implements `Node`);
   - the JVM switch alone: 652 s, and a switch every JVM would need;
   - a class-keyed dispatch.
2. **30 cases per method.** The largest method is 4,474 bytes, against the limit of 8,000.
3. **The patch changes the generator and the file it writes, not the file alone.** A build would otherwise
   regenerate the old walker the next time `Fortress.ast` or a generator changes.
4. **An audit by branch index, not by memo hits.** The fix adds no memo.
5. **The test is in Java**, because of the scalac 2.13 limit (§8).
6. **The brief's "distance stage is `tools/count-run/`" read as `tools/distance/run.sh`.** `count-run.sh`
   runs each interpreter test under walk.

**Findings.**
- The interpreted walker (§2.2).
- The shares of the repair (+267 s) and of rung C (+109 s before the fix, +65 s after) (§3).
- After the fix, about 95 % of the component's time is in the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3).
- The checker's output depends on identity hashes (§9).
- The repair removes the distance stage's crash row and adds no site (§6).
- The other methods over the limit are negligible after the fix (§2.2).

**Defects.**
- **The interpreted walker.** My change repairs it (way 1), pinned by `WalkerJUTest`. No ledger row holds it;
  the row to write:
  - claim: the generated `Walker.walk` (`FortressAst.scala`, from `ScalaAstGenerator.java`) is 31,704 bytes
    of bytecode, past HotSpot's 8,000-byte huge-method limit, so the JVM never compiles it, and every phase
    that walks a tree runs it in the interpreter;
  - status: NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, closed by the fix's commit;
  - class: implementation gap (generator, speed);
  - spec: silent;
  - reproducer: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`;
  - found by: this probe.
- **The identity-hash dependence.** A note for row 488, with the H runs' commands and outputs (§9).

**Sentences of the specification made false:** none.

**For FACTS.**
1. **The fact.** The generated AST walker's `walk` was one method over HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit, so it ran
   interpreted. With it split in order, the count stage with row 680's repair takes 352 s instead of 911 s,
   and the distance stage 931 s instead of 2,375 s, with identical output.
   - What it means: row 680's line can land under the 690 s rule.
   - Test: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`.
   - Detail: §2.2 and §6.
2. **The fact.** The checker's output depends on the JVM's identity-hash sequence, because AST hashes include
   the `Class` identity hash. One extra identity hash at start reorders the api checks and the members of
   unions in messages.
   - What it means: the stages' outputs can move with an unrelated edit (row 488).
   - Command: the driver with `-Dprobe.hashes=1`.
   - Detail: §9.
3. **The fact.** Rung C's normal form costs 12 % of the count stage before the fix, 19 % after.
   - Detail: §3.

**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**
- Q1: land the walker split as its own rung ahead of row 680's line, or in the same rung?
- Q2: pursue the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3), about 95 % of what remains?
  - Ways: a memo of normalized meets shared across analyzers; fewer reductions in `Formula.and`'s fold.
- Q3: make AST hashing independent of identity hashes (row 488)? That would change iteration orders, and so
  message text, once.

**Commands worked out.**
- **JFR, read without the text dump.** A single-file Java program over `jdk.jfr.consumer.RecordingFile`
  aggregates `jdk.ExecutionSample` within an epoch window, by self, inclusive, callers or callees. A frame's
  `getType()` (Interpreted, JIT compiled, Inlined) shows which methods the JVM never compiled.
- **Methods over the limit:** a `java.lang.classfile` scan of `ProjectFortress/build` for `Code` attributes
  longer than 8,000 bytes.
- **The AST generators by hand, in scratch:**
  1. `javac -cp <scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar -d <dir>/build ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/*.java`.
  2. Copy `Fortress.ast` into `<dir>/astgen`.
  3. From there, `java -cp <dir>/build:<scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:astgen.jar edu.rice.cs.astgen.ASTGen Fortress.ast`. The `.ast` file's `customClassPath ../build` finds the generators.
- **A huge method's compile attempts:** `-XX:-DontCompileHugeMethods -XX:+PrintCompilation`.
- **Moving the identity-hash sequence:** a driver copy that calls `new Object().hashCode()` N times before
  the phases.

## 10. Decisions, findings, questions

**Decisions.**

1. I shared only answers whose computation read no context. This chooses exactness over reach. The alternatives:
   - TypeScript's rule, dualized: a true answer found under the history's cuts is true without them. It shares
     more, but it can change nested answers, and with them the per-analyzer normal forms.
   - Keys renamed apart, plus the variables' bounds, shared across analyzers.
   - Fuel or depth limits, which change answers.
   - Library-side changes: drop `IntLiteral` from `Number`'s clause, or keep `T extends Number`. These change the
     library, not the checker.
2. Only `True` and `False` are shared, not constraint formulas.
3. A hit in the analyzer's own memo counts as a context read. This is conservative.
4. The memo lives on `TraitTable`, behind its own switch, following rung M.
5. The refusal test carries the `XXX` prefix, by the team's convention.

No decision of the curator covers 1 to 5.

**Findings for the record.**

- The slowdown is recomputation, with the numbers of §2 and §3.
- The count stage on this tree takes about 300 s for the base, measured once at load 0.31. That is not "seconds",
  and the base's `checkApi FortressLibrary` takes 74 s under the fix.
- The overloading stage's error order is not fixed between runs (by reading, §7).
- Noticed by reading, not verified: `withClauseParams` decides by name whether a type variable in an excludes
  clause is in scope (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:820`). So an analyzer whose own parameter has the same name as the
  clause's could read the clause through its own bound. The fix counts that test as a context read.

**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**

- Q1: carry the fix as a rung ahead of fork 2's library half, or with it, or hold both until the distance stage's
  remaining gap (1,032 s against 819 s at the landed gate, not a pair) is also closed?
- Q2: pursue the further exact steps of §9?

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's checker-count stage: run the bytecode compiler's static checker over the
# INTERPRETER's library, with the interpreter's prelude in scope, and print the per-api
# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table holds a total; 1 if no table could be produced, or if the table holds
# no total because the run's errors are not the checker's (#stopped, below). 20 s in the
# main tree, measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The run stops after the type checker (WorldFlip -stop check), since 2026-10-24 (climb batch
# 22): the compiler's own phase order up to and including TYPECHECK, integer literal folding
# included, as the distance stage's DistanceMulti -order check. Past the checker, the code
# generator's refusals are not the checker's errors (FACTS F-34 counts them), and its first
# one throws, so a run on a library the checker passes went on into the code generator and
# printed no total. A run the checker stops runs the same phases as before; a clean check,
# a run that reached the component's check and ended rc 0 with no error line, reads as 0.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file; its -stop check added 2026-10-24) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of
# perf-probes/prelude/run-all.sh:33-35. A copy of a tracked source goes stale silently,
# so the checksum of the tracked one is recorded here and the table's "#shadow" line
# says whether it still matches.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false, read
# at OverloadingChecker.scala:77), since 2026-09-27 (climb batch 7). The memo is keyed on
# declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api's
# overloading check runs (perf-probes/nat/triage.md section 1; FACTS.md, "The hidden
# layer, classified"); with it off every build gives one count. The table's "#cache"
# row says so. On the tree of 2026-09-27 the count is 62 with the memo on and off,
# because the FortressLibrary api stops before its overloading check.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #api        one row per api the checker checked, with that api's error count
#   #total      the errors that the run's last "File X has N errors." line counts, or 0 for
#               a clean check (above)
#   #locations  the distinct file:line those errors were reported at
#   #stopped    in place of #total and #locations, when that line counts errors that the
#               checker did not report: no api's check reported an error and the checker
#               never reached the component, so the library stopped at parse or name
#               binding, before the apis' check or between it and the component's. It names
#               the target, that line and the files the errors were reported in. The gate's
#               checker_compare reads a table with no #total row as NO TOTAL, red.
#   #crash      the first OverloadingChecker crash the checker survived, or none
#   #cache      whether the overloading checker's memo is on (it is off: above)
#   #shadow     whether the instrumented copy still matches the tracked StaticChecker
# test_run.py beside this script tests these readings on canned run outputs.
set -u
STOCK_SHA=16e6e11df9341a67038b7d7cc9f0d7bb5e5a6149019f09e92545a8b646363a0b   # ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java, 2026-09-22
OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi

# 1. build the driver and the instrumented checker against the tree's own classpath
javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" \
      "$D/WorldFlip.java" "$D/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \

fi

# 2. run the compiler phase order through the checker over the interpreter's library under a
#    private cache
( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 10 900 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" \
       -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=$OVERLOAD_CACHE \
       -cp "$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" WorldFlip -stop check "$TARGET" ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
RC=$?
# A clean check: the checker reached the component, and the run ended rc 0 with no error line.
CLEAN=

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.
